title: Earl Bostic and the alto players of the day
summary: He recalls Vinson, Tab Smith, Jordan and Bostic as individual stylists, and Bostic's advice on mouthpiece and reed.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Listening to you now, it’s obvious how influential Charlie Parker was, but you’ve also talked about listening to a lot of alto saxophonists who were active then...
Talk about those people, and how you assimilated...

Well, those people were so great. Every one of those people had a different style. See, not like it is today when everybody plays the same way. But back then, they had a different style. Earl Bostic was the greatest technician I’ve ever heard on a saxophone. He could play three octaves. I eventually got to talk to him, and he told me what mouthpiece I should use, and reed, and I’ve been using them ever 1957.
Meyer #6 mouthpiece, #2½ reed. Now I’m down to 1½ because old age has caught up with me, so...
